# Three-way todo comparison

Recorded on 2026-09-12 after the user requested fresh subagents with v3.1.1 installed, current v5 installed, and without AER. The prior two-arm result and apps were preserved. This was a separate known-task regression comparison following the UI-delivery change, not a held-out efficacy study.

## Protocol and identity

- Three fresh GPT-6 Astra agents, low effort, one implementation attempt per treatment and a separate ten-minute allowance. The task and prompt template were unchanged from the previous comparison, apart from assigned paths and ports.
- The ten requirement groups and concrete evaluation cases were frozen before dispatch. All relevant exercised cases had to pass for a group to pass; focus loss and revised-draft loss retained their earlier scoring interpretation.
- Sessions used separate directories and origins with no inherited task history. They shared the host and base agent instructions; directory/prompt separation was not OS-level isolation.
- V3.1.1 used its actual release installer from commit `c1353c7993b4ff78e09963b01207d8b2d2c5d29e`. V5 used the then-current uncommitted working tree with the direct UI interaction clause. No application was repaired after submission.

The [results artifact](../evidence/5.0.0-todo-three-way.json) is a byte-identical copy of the local result, without personal filesystem paths. It records each group, observed failures, artifact measurements and evidence limits. Local application and instruction inventories were hashed before dispatch and after submission; protected inputs and submitted apps were unchanged during grading. This public record does not bundle the local apps or full browser trace.

## Results

| Treatment | Execution | Exercised groups passed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V3.1.1 | Completed within allowance | 10/10, with reset qualification below |
| Revised v5 | Completed within allowance | 10/10 |
| Without AER | Completed within allowance | 8/10 |

The baseline retained an old retry proposal: after a failed add, changing the draft and retrying saved the old title and cleared the revision. It also replaced focused list controls without assigning a useful successor after toggle, reopen, Save, Cancel/Escape, deletion and filtered removal. Both rule versions handled these exercised cases correctly. All three passed ordinary task management, composed search/filtering, exact persistence, invalid-data detection, and narrow-layout reachability.

The evaluator directly exercised the browser, inspected actual localStorage values, injected quota-style write failures, used keyboard actions, measured each 390px iframe, and inspected source and file hashes. Agent-authored checks were not rerun or treated as blanket proof. All agents added optional permanent checks; assertion counts and artifact sizes do not establish verification efficiency. Exact tokens, cost and compute time were unavailable.

## Execution qualifications

- The initial third spawn was rejected at the host's thread limit. A fresh baseline started after v5 completed, with its own full allowance. The rejected spawn was not a model attempt, and staggered start times were not used to rank speed.
- Three v3.1.1 corruption snapshots preceded module readiness. Those observations remained unresolved until the recovery control was visibly present; no model attempt or app was changed.
- V3.1.1's native reset confirmation stalled the browser driver, which exposed no usable dialog handle. An opt-in evaluator adapter accepted the disposable-data confirmation and observed the original app reset the stored value. Native dialog handling remains unverified; this qualification accompanies its score. Original and adapted evaluator hashes are in the result artifact.

V5 tied v3.1.1 in this run. One small task, one observation per treatment, an unblinded evaluator, reused task knowledge and a qualified browser check do not establish superiority, causality, broad engineering quality or fulfillment of every grievance. No general efficacy or savings claim is made.
